original_question: Can a mutation in the gene that encodes connexin 31, which is associated with erythrokeratodermia variabilis, also cause non-syndromic deafness?

final_qi.question: Can a mutation in the gene that encodes connexin 31, which is associated with erythrokeratodermia variabilis, also cause non-syndromic deafness?
final_qi.long_answer: The gene that encodes connexin 31 is GJB3. Pathogenic variants in GJB3 were first recognised as a cause of the skin disorder erythrokeratodermia variabilis (EKV). Independent of any skin manifestations, several studies have shown that other (or sometimes the same) GJB3 mutations can affect cochlear gap-junction channels and produce isolated, non-syndromic sensorineural hearing loss. Such hearing loss has been catalogued as autosomal dominant DFNA2B and, in some families, as autosomal recessive or digenic DFNB1-type deafness. Therefore, a mutation in the connexin 31 gene that is implicated in EKV can indeed also cause non-syndromic deafness.

final_answer.long_answer: Variants in GJB3, the gene encoding the gap-junction protein connexin 31 and classically linked to erythrokeratodermia variabilis, have also been documented in multiple families with autosomal dominant or recessive non-syndromic sensorineural hearing loss. Hence a connexin 31 mutation can indeed cause non-syndromic deafness.
